content.title: Time for the module review
content.body:
You've finished the lessons in this module. Now it's time to review the big ideas.

This quiz has 5 questions covering:

• How computers follow instructions
• Why bugs happen
• What algorithms are
• How programmers tackle big problems

Take your time. There is no timer, and every question includes an explanation after you answer.

quiz.question: In the Input → Processing → Output pattern, what is the "Processing" step?

options.text: Taking information into the program
Showing a result on the screen
The computer working with the input to figure something out
Writing the code

quiz.explanation: Processing is when the computer takes the input and does something with it before producing an output.

quiz.question:
A robot is given these steps:

1. Pour the juice
2. Open the bottle

What will the robot do?

options.text: Open the bottle first because it figures out the order
Pour the juice without any trouble
Ask a human to fix the steps
Try to pour from a bottle that's still closed

quiz.explanation: Robots and computers run steps in the exact order they're written — they won't rearrange them.

quiz.question: A program does something the programmer didn't want it to do. What do we call that?

options.text: A program that ran out of room
A bug
A feature that's hard to use
A broken computer

quiz.explanation: A bug is a mistake in the code that makes a program behave in a way the programmer didn't expect. Every programmer writes bugs — finding them is part of the job.

quiz.question: Kai walks down a line of kids looking for the tallest one, remembering the tallest he's seen so far. What is Kai using?

options.text: A type of computer chip
A kind of bug
An algorithm
A programming language

quiz.explanation: An algorithm is a clear, step-by-step plan for solving a problem — exactly what Kai is doing.

quiz.question: You want to build a whole quiz game, but the idea feels too big. What do programmers do in this situation?

options.text: Try to write all the code at once
Give up because it's too hard
Wait for someone else to build it
Break the problem into smaller steps

quiz.explanation: Programmers handle big problems by splitting them into smaller pieces and solving one piece at a time.
